title: He looked like a “good man.”
paragraphs: But heaven said, he still needed saving.
Because this is where it gets uncomfortable…
Cornelius wasn’t the villain in the story.
He was the one we would admire.
That’s the tension most people don’t want to face.
Because if a man like that still needed the Gospel…
what does that say about us?
You can build a life that impresses people…
and still stand empty before God.
You can give, serve, lead, stay clean, stay disciplined…
and still be trusting yourself instead of Christ.
But subtle confidence in your own goodness.
A heart that says, “I’m not that bad.”
“Cornelius… was a devout man who feared God… gave alms generously… and prayed continually to God.” (Acts 10:2)
That sounds like someone ready for heaven.
Cornelius needed to hear about Jesus.
Peter stands in his house and says:
“Everyone who believes in Him receives forgiveness of sins through His name.” (Acts 10:43)
Because the Gospel doesn’t negotiate with your résumé.
It says your best is still not enough.
“for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God” (Romans 3:23)
Not just the broken ones in public.
That includes the quiet good people.
The ones who never made headlines for the wrong reasons.
And here’s the part many miss.
He didn’t say, “But I already pray.”
And while Peter was still speaking…
“The Holy Spirit fell on all who heard the word.” (Acts 10:44)
You don’t climb your way to God.
Some scholars interpret this moment as a divine declaration that the Gospel is not limited by ethnicity, tradition, or religious background—but fully open to all who believe in Christ.
There is no “type” of person who qualifies more.
And there is no “good version” of you that replaces Jesus.
Let me speak directly to the hidden place.
The place where no one sees.
And salvation was never meant to be built on you.
Not just in actions—but in nature.
No amount of effort can erase sin.
But God, in mercy, sent His Son.
Jesus lived the life you could not live.
“Repent and turn back, that your sins may be blotted out.” (Acts 3:19)
Because the most dangerous place to be…
A good man can still be lost.
A seeking heart still needs the Savior.
And the moment you truly believe—
Have you actually surrendered to Jesus?
Or are you still trusting your “good life”?
If something inside you is breaking right now…
Type “I SURRENDER” if you’re choosing Jesus today.
Or “OPEN MY HEART” if you’re ready to stop pretending and start following Him for real.
